text:
For about six minutes Seattle had the start it wanted. Kaapo Kakko tipped in a power-play goal at 5:57 of the first, and the Kraken arrived in San Jose carrying Berkly Catton's first NHL hat trick from the night before. Then the Sharks scored four straight, and the rest of the night was Seattle trying to climb out of that hole.

Michael Misa answered 29 seconds after Kakko. Nolan Allan put San Jose ahead on a shot that, by our numbers, had a 2% chance of going in. Macklin Celebrini blasted a power-play slap shot past Philipp Grubauer late in the first, and Ivar Stenberg, the second overall pick this summer, made it 4-1 on another power play in the second. Dmitry Orlov assisted on three of the four and took the first star.

Seattle's response was real. Matty Beniers scored for a third straight game, set up by Mackie Samoskevich and Kakko, and Ryan Winterton cut it to 4-3 with three minutes left in the second. The Kraken had the better of the chances overall: 3.44 expected goals (the quality of their chances) to 2.70, and in our replays of every shot they win this game 62% of the time. Alex Nedeljkovic held the line, finishing 0.44 goals better than the shots he faced deserved, and his stop on Catton in the final minute was the save that mattered most. Grubauer went the other way, 1.3 goals worse than expected on 29 shots.

The difference was special teams. San Jose went 2 for 3 on the power play; Seattle went 1 for 2 despite creating more on it (1.02 expected goals to 0.60). Alison Lukan of the Kraken's own coverage reported that Lane Lambert called the penalty kill "the elephant in the room" after the game. Two power-play goals against in a one-goal loss is how that phrase gets earned.

For the Sharks, it is another night where the kids carried it: Celebrini with a goal and an assist, Stenberg the same, Misa with five shots. Tyler Toffoli's missed breakaway in the second, a 29% look that went wide, was the one chance that could have made it comfortable.
headline: Sharks' power play outlasts a Kraken push
